steps: Create a fine-grained token while signed in as the account that should open the pull requests.
Repository access: the repositories you work on.
Permissions: Pull requests = Read and write, Contents = Read. Metadata = Read is added for you.
A classic token works too: tick repo.
Choose Create API token with scopes, and pick the app Bitbucket.
Tick read:user, read:repository, read:pullrequest and write:pullrequest (Atlassian shows each with :bitbucket added).
Enter the email address of the same Atlassian account.
Choose Create API token, without scopes. Lantern calls your Jira site address directly, which scoped tokens do not allow.
There is nothing to tick: the token acts as you, with your Jira permissions.
Site address: the one in your browser when Jira is open, like https://your-company.atlassian.net.

permissionConsent.message: Let Lantern allow Claude's delegate commands in {project}?
permissionConsent.detail: Lantern would add rules to this project's .claude/settings.local.json (a file git ignores) so background delegates can run git status, commit, fetch, push to feat, fix, docs and chore branches, and Lantern's skill scripts without asking each time. It also lets them reset a worktree to origin/<branch>. Nothing is written if you decline, and you are not asked again for this project.

micPatch.message: Enable the microphone in the Claude Code extension?
micPatch.detail: Lantern would edit extension.js inside the Claude Code extension in ~/.vscode-server/extensions, a file that belongs to a third party, and keep a copy of the original next to it (extension.js.ccm-bak). The change removes the check that turns voice input off in a remote editor. It can stop working or break the extension when the extension updates, and Anthropic does not endorse it. Nothing is changed if you cancel.
